newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. lawmaker urges ending China trade status.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. lawmaker urges ending China trade status.

text.p: An influential House of Representatives Republican leader urged President Bill Clinton on Monday to revoke China's so-called trade privileges, citing Beijing's record on human rights, weapons sales and copyright piracy.

In a two-page letter to Clinton, Representative Bill Paxon of New York, chairman of the House Republican leadership, said current U.S. policy had yielded only "a Chinese regime which thumbs its nose at the United States and places its heal on the neck of freedom."

Paxon, a close ally of House Speaker Newt Gingrich, said that denying "Most Favoured Nation" trade status "would send a message to China that the United States believes in something more than the blind pursuit of trade."
On Sunday, Gingrich, Republican of Georgia, predicted "a weaker vote than it was a year ago" when the House voted 286 to 141 to back Clinton's renewal of China's trade status.
Clinton has said he supports China's MFN renewal for another year. He must inform Congress formally by June 3.

To reverse such a presidential recommendation, the House and Senate would have to pass a joint resolution disapproving of the policy by Aug. 31. And to reverse an expected presidential veto, both chambers would have to approve such a resolution by a two-thirds margin.
